niche.diet: Carnivore: drifting carcasses, brujula, cuarteta, and young grazers that wade.
niche.active: Feeds at low tide when water recedes, ambushing stranded prey and waders.

links: Turbid shallows dense with kelp and jagged basalt
Limbs would snag and betray position in three-dimensional tangles
Undulatory propulsion allows silent navigation through obstacles

skill.effect: When navigating kelp thickets and rocky terrain, it darts forward with sudden, powerful bursts of speed.

chains.weakness: Slower acceleration on open, flat sand.
observe: Sees it slide through kelp without disturbing silt
Sees it coil tightly before striking
Hears a faint wet drag followed by a sharp crack

journal.en: It flows through the dark water like smoke.

plausibility.summary: In F20 turbid shelf habitat, obstacle-rich three-dimensional cover favours undulatory swimmers over walking limbs; F24 shared vertebrate biochemistry allows a limbless elasmobranch- or anguilliform-grade plan. At 3.2 m and ~85 kg the mass is within range of large moray-grade predators and below island-wide apex budgets (D26), so it can be shelf-top without breaking pyramid rules (D25). Dense air (F4) mainly matters on exposed crawling, not underwater thrust.

Dense air (F4) mainly matters on exposed crawling, not underwater thrust.

analogues.organism: Green moray (Gymnothorax funebris) and giant moray (G. javanicus): long muscular hydrostat, reef-structure navigation without paired limbs.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Prey generate weak bioelectric fields through gill movement

observe: Snout twitches rapidly when prey is hidden
Tracks movement in opaque water with no visual cue
Sees it ignore decoy bubbles to strike the real target

journal.en: It reads the silence where eyes fail.

plausibility.summary: F20 explicitly shifts shallow marine foraging toward non-visual senses; weak dipole fields from gill ventilation and muscle activity in small prey (brújula, cuarteta, juvenile filter feeders) are detectable at close range with ampullae-like organs, as on Earth. Rostral clustering improves aiming in <10 m visibility without requiring unreal field strengths.

links: 3.2m tidal range exposes wide shelf at low tide

journal.en: The water leaves, but the hunter remains.

chains.trait: Dense red muscle for high metabolism
links: 1.6 bar atmosphere raises dissolved O2 in seawater
Higher partial pressure supports massive aerobic tissue
Enables rapid strikes and quick recovery between lunges

journal.en: It burns the air itself to fuel the chase.

relations.note: Ambushed in kelp thickets and tidal pools.
Snapped up in the shallows' turbid margins.
Filtered sifons are caught before they retreat to deep water.
Juvenile filter-feeders are taken from drifting carcass clouds.

changelog.what: removed rejected references and non-existent root facts (roots recovered from the derivation items cited in the links, else F27)

temperament: Patient ambush predator, irritable when disturbed.
secrets: Electroreceptive rostrum tip can be harvested to build 'Sense' gear (Passive/Basic) that highlights prey in water.
Its tough, slick skin yields a 'Hydrodynamic' part that reduces drag (Defence) for aquatic builds.
Found near high-tide carcass lines: it caches large kills in kelp mats for later.
moments: At dawn, when the tide drops to its lowest, it drags its massive body across the exposed, glistening shelf. It stops perfectly still in a shallow pool, its rostrum twitching like a radar dish, waiting for the first grazing zanco to lower its head to drink. The only sound is the wet drag of its belly and the distant crash of the surf.

journal.en: It moves like smoke and strikes like a whip.
The tide retreats, and so does its patience.
